text: Why does the CPG lab choose a supra-critical (rho = 1.25) reservoir instead of a sub-critical (rho < 1) one, even though the latter guarantees the echo state property?
choices: A rho < 1 reservoir would violate ridge regression's assumptions and fail to converge
Only rho > 1 keeps the reservoir linear, which FORCE requires

A sub-critical reservoir has fading memory and relaxes to rest with no input, so it cannot self-sustain a rhythm; the rho > 1 reservoir supplies intrinsic, self-sustaining dynamics that FORCE sculpts into the target gait
rho > 1 is needed so the eight readout channels stay mutually orthogonal
explanation: For autonomous generation there is no external input, so a fading-memory (rho < 1) reservoir would simply decay to rest and produce no rhythm. A supra-critical reservoir has its own persistent (chaotic) activity; FORCE stabilizes and shapes that activity into a target limit cycle, which is the lab's stated key insight. Option 1 is false (rho > 1 makes the dynamics more nonlinear/chaotic, not linear); options 0 and 3 are fabricated rationales.
